narrative.heading: A path into heart health
narrative.text: Nieca Goldberg’s interest in cardiology began when her father developed heart disease at a young age. Her NYU biography describes summer work with a cardiologist and a later decision to focus on women after encountering dismissive assumptions about their heart health during residency. Questions from patients also shaped her interest in making space for dialogue: she describes beginning visits by asking what patients want to discuss.

The profile lists English and French and source-stated, location-dependent insurance information; languages have not been independently assessed, and the exact plan is not confirmed. narrative.heading: A childhood spark and human connection
narrative.text: Anu Lala-Trindade traces her wish to become a cardiologist to a childhood encounter with her grandmother’s illness. In Mount Sinai’s June 25, 2021 Heart to Heart interview, she recalls feeling her grandmother’s pulse and becoming fascinated by the connection between the heartbeat and a person’s life. She also describes the importance of human connection in caring for patients and supporting families through uncertainty.

access.heading: Before contacting Mount Sinai
access.text: Mount Sinai lists the Lauder Family Cardiovascular Ambulatory Center at 1190 Fifth Avenue, First Floor, New York, NY 10029, phone 212-241-7300, adult care, English and video visits. The page listed accepting-new-patient status when observed on October 15, 2026; this is not a capacity guarantee. Insurance information is source-stated and location-specific; confirm the exact plan and current clinician participation. Fees and referral requirements are not established here.
